message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | The first book in the globally‑famous Harry Potter series. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment, continuing Harry’s adventures at Hogwarts. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Focuses on the formation of Dumbledore’s Army. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Explores Voldemort’s past and the Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | The epic conclusion to the series. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, a political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | The first book in the Cormoran Strike detective series. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |
| **Cormoran Strike Series (overall)** | 2013‑2023 | A total of 10 books (including the “Cormoran Strike” and “Cormoran Strike: The Cormoran Strike” sub‑series) under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith. |

These titles represent the bulk of Rowling’s most widely read and commercially successful works. If you’re interested in a particular genre or period of her writing, let me know and I can narrow it down further!
